judgments.reasoning_cat1: The recital limits the licence to marks used 'solely for the purposes of operating and promoting' the facilities 'all in the Morton Territories', and 'solely for the purposes of' is a purpose limitation whose reach is contestable. As a recital it is not itself operative, but its wording is broad and undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against the operative grant in 2(a), which expressly allows promotion, advertising, marketing and broadcasting of the facilities 'anywhere in the world', so the recital's territorial confinement and the operative carve-out point in different directions (classic 2.3). The recital also speaks of selling merchandise 'in the Hotel/Casinos or Casinos' while 2(b)(v) permits Internet sales.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition sweeps in 'all confusingly similar names, marks and logos, including, without limiting the generality of the foregoing' such names as 'Rock Cafe', 'Hard Rock' and 'derivations thereof' — a catch-all against enumerated specifics whose outer edge is genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because 'Hard Rock' itself is inside this reserved definition, it is hard to reconcile with 2(b)(vi), 2(b)(ix) and 6(c), which let Licensee use 'Hard Rock' plus other designations; the carve-out for the Exhibit A/B marks does not cleanly resolve that overlap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition simply incorporates Exhibit A, and its qualifier 'except as expressly provided herein' leaves open which other Hard Rock rights are pulled back in.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit A lists both 'Hard Rock Casino' and 'Hard Rock Hotel', so the Hotel Marks overlap the Casino Marks defined by reference to Exhibit B in 1(c), an internal inconsistency that matters for 2(b)(i) and 3(a).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Purely referential definition; the only soft edge is 'except as expressly provided herein'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit B ('Hard Rock Casino') duplicates an entry in Exhibit A, so the two mark sets defined in 1(b) and 1(c) are not mutually exclusive despite the agreement treating them as distinct in 2(b)(i) and 3(a).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All-inclusive place for lodging', 'indoor corridors' and 'a variety of amenities' are vague criteria with no boundary, and one can name 'all-inclusive' and 'variety of amenities' as the ambiguous terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The definition feeds 1(f), 2(b)(i) and the Nevada carve-out in 3(a), where whether a property is a 'Hotel' decides who may use the marks; no direct contradiction, but its vagueness propagates.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A substantial source of revenue and its principal function' is a vague and possibly internally doubled test, and 'such as slot machines, gaming tables and the like' is an ejusdem generis catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with 2(b)(i) (Casino Marks may be used at a casino without a hotel) and 2(b)(ix) (riverboats), and the riverboat sentence here duplicates that treatment without conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Immediately adjoining contiguous facility' and 'part of the same "Hard Rock" complex/development' are undefined spatial tests capable of more than one reading.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the gateway to 2(b)(i)'s prohibition on hotel-only use and to 3(a)'s reservation of hotel-without-casino rights to Licensor, so its looseness could unsettle that allocation but nothing squarely contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short compositional definition with no ambiguous term of its own.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Confining 'Hard Rock Hotel' to the Morton Territories sits oddly with 3(a)'s prohibition on Licensor owning 'a Hard Rock Hotel in the State of Nevada' and with 2(b)(vii)'s reference to 'other Hard Rock Hotels', but the readings can be harmonised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Straightforward compositional definition built from defined terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2(a), 2(b)(i) and 2(b)(ix); no provision pulls against it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite and mechanical; 'and/or' is the only slack.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The territorial limit here sits against 2(a)'s permission to promote and broadcast 'Hard Rock Hotel/Casinos' anywhere in the world, but that is a workable reading rather than a contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed three-item collective definition with no catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used in 8(a) and 2(b)(vii); the fact that it includes Licensor's cafes and Licensee's hotels makes 2(b)(vii)'s 'any other Hard Rock Facility' broad, but nothing contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The territorial description contains obvious mechanical errors ('fifty (SO) mile radius form the City Hall') and vague reference points ('other similarly recognized civic center structure located reasonably near the geographic center'), and states 'west of the Mississippi River' is itself contestable for river-straddling states.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This term drives 2(a), 2(b)(iv), 3(a) and 8(a)(1); no other provision contradicts it, though 3(a)'s Nevada carve-out assumes Nevada is inside the territory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any and all services provided by Licensee in connection with or relating to the operation of' is an extremely broad, boundary-free formulation, and the text carries an OCR/typographical slip ('Hotei/Casinos').
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its breadth interacts with 4(a) quality standards and 2(a)'s worldwide promotion/broadcast carve-out — whether ancillary ventures are 'Licensed Services' would matter there — but no clause squarely contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any and all personal property, products and merchandise bearing the Hard Rock Hotel Marks or the Hard Rock Casino Marks' turns on whether goods bearing 'Hard Rock' plus some other designation bear the defined Marks at all — a nameable ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It governs 2(b)(iv), (v), (vii) and 6(c), and the interaction with 6(c)'s ban on merchandise bearing 'Hard Rock' location designations makes the category's edge genuinely contested.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A simple party definition, though including 'successors, assigns or transferees' is broad.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12 gives the Licensor notice address as 'Hard Rock Cafe International (DEL), Inc.' rather than Rank Licensing, Inc., a mismatch that this definition only partly cures through 'successors'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The grant is 'exclusive ... only in the Morton Territories and solely in connection with' listed activities, then carves out worldwide 'promotion, advertising or marketing (not including the sale of merchandise) and broadcasting' — the scope of that parenthetical and of 'broadcasting' is precisely the kind of line two parties read differently.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be squared with the recital's 'solely ... all in the Morton Territories', with 2(b)(iv)-(v) on where Licensed Products may be sold, and with 3(a)'s reservation to Licensor of hotel-without-casino rights 'anywhere in the world', which cuts against the stated exclusivity.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two crisp sentences keyed to defined terms; little internal slack beyond the 1(f) definition it invokes.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It complements 3(a) (Licensor keeps hotel-only rights) but depends on Exhibit A, which lists 'Hard Rock Casino' among the Hotel Marks, muddying the hotel/casino split.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The modifier placement is ambiguous: 'any restaurant in any Hard Rock Hotel/Casino or Hard Rock Casino, or anywhere else that is confusingly similar' may qualify all restaurants or only those 'anywhere else', and 'confusingly similar to a Hard Rock Cafe restaurant' is itself a vague standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The second sentence expressly preserves 'other types of restaurants', which cures much of the tension; 6(c)'s ban on confusingly similar designations runs in the same direction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Licensor shall retain the sole right to apply for ... registration' sits next to 'Licensor shall consent to any request by Licensee', and 'best efforts' plus 'reasonably likely to affect' are open-textured.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The agency fallback is expressly carved out of Section 13's no-agency rule, which shows the drafters harmonised it; residual tension with 6(b)'s bar on Licensee filings remains.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Stand alone merchandise outlet', 'contiguous to' and above all 'Licensed Products must always bear the geographic location where sold' are the terms most obviously capable of competing readings, and the sentence restricting Licensor is a one-sided fragment.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with 2(b)(v) (Internet sales bearing an Internet address as the 'location'), 2(b)(vi)-(vii) (Beach Club/Athletic Club designations replacing the geographic word) and 6(c) (no merchandise bearing such designations), a cluster that does not cleanly cohere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Bear the Internet address as the Licensed Products' location' and the exception 'except for Hard Rock Internet access kits' are odd, dated formulations whose application to a modern online store is genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the express exception to 2(b)(iv)'s retail-only and geographic-legend rules and overlaps 8(b)'s web-site allocation, so the three provisions together leave the permitted scope of online merchandising contestable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Other designations such as "Beach Club" or "Athletic Club"' is an unbounded catch-all illustrated by two specifics, and 'only within the confines of' and 'not for the sale of merchandise' are further contestable limits.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interlocks with 2(b)(iv)'s geographic-legend rule, with 2(b)(vii)-(viii) (which treat the very same Exhibit D/E designations inconsistently) and with 3(d)'s bar on qualifying words 'other than geographical designations'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The designations identified on Exhibit D and currently in use at the Las Vegas Hard Rock Hotel' fixes rights by reference to an undated factual state, and the merchandise sentence's eighteen-month cut-off is drafted against that moving baseline.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit D and Exhibit E list the same designations (Beach Club / Athletic Club), yet this clause permits their continuing use in other properties while 2(b)(viii) requires that they 'forever cease' after eighteen months — a genuine internal inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Whatever merchandise is currently being sold' and 'such designations' are defined only by an unrecorded snapshot at signing, which is inherently hard to apply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It directly collides with 2(b)(vii), which permits the same Exhibit D/E designations to be used in other Hard Rock Hotels and Casinos, and with 2(b)(vi)'s standing permission to use 'Beach Club' or 'Athletic Club' designations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Certain terminology, such as "Riverboat"' is an open illustration, though the conditional ('the jurisdiction ... requires') is reasonably concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Permitting 'Hard Rock Riverboat' within the circle logo is in tension with 2(b)(vi)'s rule that Licensee 'shall not replace the word "Hotel" or "Casino" with any other designation' absent written consent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It combines an absolute reservation with several exceptions, including 'affiliated entity' and 'a Hotel facility that does not include a Casino', terms whose edges are contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Licensor's right to use the Hotel Marks 'anywhere in the world' for a casino-free hotel is hard to square with 2(a)'s grant of an exclusive licence in the Morton Territories, and the Nevada carve-out is separately enforced by 11(a).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard no-challenge and goodwill acknowledgement; the phrase 'during the Term of this Agreement or thereafter' is the only loose element.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Term' is capitalised but 9(a) makes the licence perpetual, so 'or thereafter' has little work to do; 5(d) meanwhile contemplates litigated validity disputes, a mild counterpoint.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, conventional goodwill-inurement acknowledgement with no ambiguous operative term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3(a), 3(b) and 4(f); nothing in the instrument pulls against it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Dominate, modify or qualify' is a vague trio and 'other than geographical designations' is an expressio unius carve-out excluding everything else.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That exclusive geographic carve-out conflicts with 2(b)(vi)-(vii), which expressly allow non-geographic designations such as 'Beach Club' and 'Athletic Club' to replace the geographic word.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence residual covenant tied back to the agreement's own provisions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It restates 2(a) and 3(a) and its 'unless the parties agree otherwise in writing' aligns with 22 and 23; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Good quality at least as high as the quality of similar goods presently sold' and 'equal to and commensurate with the existing products and services' are benchmarks fixed to an unrecorded 1996 baseline and are genuinely vague.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the trigger for the 5(a) arbitration mechanism and is qualified by 4(f)'s statement that quality rights exist 'solely' to protect goodwill, so its content shapes those clauses without contradicting them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable access', 'reasonable notice' and 'will not cause any disruption' are soft but conventional inspection standards.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits 4(a), 4(c) and 4(f) and the no-interference framing in 13; no conflicting provision found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is syntactically garbled — 'furnish or render ... requested Licensed Services, representative samples on the premises of each Licensed Product' — leaving unclear what must be produced and where.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is ancillary to 4(b)'s inspection right and 4(a)'s standard, and nothing elsewhere contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, standard legal-compliance covenant with no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2(b)(ix)'s accommodation of regulatory terminology; no tension identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Wherever the same may be used with reasonable convenience' and 'the appropriate notice of registration' are vague obligations whose breach point is hard to fix.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It applies to advertising that 2(a) permits worldwide, and to designations regulated by 2(b)(vi); a mandatory-use rule sits a little awkwardly with those restrictions but is not contradicted.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Solely to ensure the quality' is an interpretive limitation on Licensor's rights, and 'all rights ... to monitor and intervene' is undefined but the sentence's thrust is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates the last sentence of Section 13 and could be read to cut down the approval rights conferred by 2(b)(iii), 2(b)(vi) and 4(b)-(c), which are not purely quality-driven.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The arbitral scope — disputes 'regarding the failure of Licensee to conform to any provision of quality control' — is narrow but its boundary is contestable, and 'proscribed' for 'prescribed' is a mechanical slip.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be reconciled with 5(d)'s exclusion of everything 'not specifically identified hereinabove', with 11(a)'s promise of court injunctions and with 14's New York forum clause, since 5(a) sends alternating arbitrations to California.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Broad but plainly worded grant of remedial power to the arbitrators; 'whatsoever that is deemed appropriate' is loose.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Arbitral power to grant permanent injunctions overlaps 11(a)'s allocation of injunctive relief to 'a court of competent jurisdiction', a mild duplication rather than a contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Procedural and definite: thirty business days, binding, enforceable under New York law.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coheres with 14's New York governing law; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with 5(a), the boundary between arbitrable quality disputes and court-bound 'validity' disputes is unstable, and 14 routes non-Section-5 claims to New York courts while 5(a) may site an arbitration in California.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Best efforts to protect' is a classic vague standard with no metric or specified conduct.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps 6(d)'s detailed enforcement allocation and 2(b)(iii)'s 'best efforts' registration duty, which supply content rather than contradict it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad negative covenant; 'affect the ownership of or encumber, damage, dilute or modify' is expansive but its direction is unmistakable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against 2(b)(iii), which contemplates Licensee preparing and filing registration documents as Licensor's agent if Licensor defaults, a permitted exception this clause does not mention.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The second sentence permits use of the 'Hard Rock' designation 'to identify locations, services or areas' but bars any merchandise bearing 'such designations', and what counts as 'such designations' versus a licensed mark is a nameable ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The merchandise ban is hard to square with 2(b)(vii), which expressly allows merchandise bearing Exhibit D designations for eighteen months, and with 2(b)(iv)-(vi) governing designations on Licensed Products.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Each party may sue 'at its own cost' and keep recoveries, yet Licensor 'will always have full control of any joint proceedings' with costs and recoveries shared — 'joint proceedings' is undefined and the two regimes are not sequenced.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The equal-sharing sentence is limited to 'within Morton's Territories' while the individual-action sentence is not, and the closing agency disclaimer echoes Section 13; the pieces sit uneasily but can be harmonised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sided, uncapped indemnity covering 'any suits, loss and damage arising out of any service or act ... or in relation to' the Marks, whose reach — including Licensor's own fault — is contestable and would be construed against the drafter.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: There is no reciprocal indemnity despite Licensor's warranty of ownership in 2(a) and its Nevada covenant in 3(a), leaving an asymmetry rather than a contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'When practical and appropriate' is an escape hatch that may swallow the obligation, and the table-display sentence says the display must be 'reasonably acceptable to Licensor' when Licensor is the party supplying it — an apparent mechanical error for 'Licensee'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the only affirmative cross-promotion duty and fits 8(a)(3) and 8(b); no other provision contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A specific attribution obligation triggered by 'any book written or sponsored by Licensor or its affiliates which describes the Hard Rock Facilities and/or history' — broad trigger, but definite content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the agreement addresses publications; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Same size and style' is a concrete, testable requirement; the conditional 'which identifies all locations' is the only soft element.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 8(a)(1) and 8(b); nothing contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An agreement merely 'to discuss the possibility' of sponsorship is an agreement to agree with no ascertainable obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It adds nothing that conflicts with the rest of Section 8 or with 13's no-joint-venture rule, though the latter limits how far joint sponsorship could go.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Licensor may develop ... except that Licensee may develop' is an oddly framed allocation that does not say whether Licensee's right is exclusive as to its properties, and 'other Hard Rock Facilities as they may develop' is loose.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Web pages inevitably intersect 2(b)(v)'s Internet-sales rules and 2(a)'s worldwide promotion carve-out, and the three provisions do not together settle who may sell online or where.
